 4. On 18-2-2008 the decree-holder filed family Execution case No. 3 of 2008 in the Family Court with a separate application for condo nation of delay of six years, four months and ten days. On 13-3-2008 the Execution case was admitted for hearing by condoning such delay, which was affirmed in Revision. 

 "S. 48 of the CP Code provides the maximum of 12 years during which a decree retains its life of excitability whereas article 182 of the Limitation Act provides a period of 3 years from the date of decree for putting the decree into execution which means if the decree is not put into execution within 3 years from the date of the last order made on a application for execution of the decree it is barred and becomes non-executable. 

 8. The learned Advocate appearing for opposite party No. 1 opposes the Rule and submits that Limitation Act is applicable in the proceedings initiated under the Family Court ordinance, 1985. He adds that decree holder was prevented by sufficient cause not to file the execution case in time therefore such delay was rightly condoned. 

 11. Ongoing to materials on record it transpires that Family Suit was decreed on 17-5-2001, against which the defendant filed Family Appeal No. 4 of 2001 and it was withdrawn on 8-8-2001. The Family execution case was filed on 18-2-2008 with a separate application for condonation of delay. It is stated in the application that on the plea of compromise the decree holder was taken to the conjugal home on 8-8-2001. About six years she was leading conjugal life. 

 Subsequently after torture she was drove out from the conjugal home on 9-8-2007. She reported the same to local chairman, who ultimately arranged an arbitration wherein judgment debtor deposited Taka 60,000 for payment to decree holder, but the local chairman ultimately on 17-2-2008 refused to make such payment. Thereafter on 18-2-2008 she filed the Family execution case for her decreetal amount of Taka 91,501. It is very shocking to note that the judgment debtor (husband) on the pretext of compromise took the decree holder (wife) in conjugal home and after expire of the stipulated period for filing the execution case, drove out his wife from the conjugal home, which is nothing but a new device of fraud practice upon the decree holder (wife), which in my view are the sufficient cause not to prefer execution case in time. Therefore the family Court by condoning such delay committed no error of law and the same was rightly affirmed in Revision by the impugned order. 

 Section 16. Enforcement of decrees— 

 (3) Where the decree relates to the payment of money and the decretal amount is not paid within the time specified by the Court, the decree shall on the prayer of the decree-holder to be made within a period of one year from the expiry of the time so specified, be executed— 

 (a) As a decree for money of a Civil Court under the Code, or 

 And on such execution the decreetal amount recovered shall be paid to the decree-holder. 

 (3A) For the purpose of execution of a decree under sub-section (3)(a), the Court shall be deemed to be a Civil Court and shall have all the powers of such Court under the Code.
